core_obligations: Reduce to algebraically closed fields (proof lines 18079-18091): the extensions of k and K by their algebraic closures are purely inseparable, hence universal homeomorphisms, so topological invariance identifies H^q(X, F) with H^q(X_kbar, F_kbar) and likewise over K; one may therefore assume k and K algebraically closed.

Apply smooth base change (proof lines 18092-18095): with both fields algebraically closed, K is a filtered colimit of smooth k-algebras, so the statement becomes a special case of the smooth base change theorem as reformulated in the general base change lemma, giving assertion (1).

Deduce assertion (2) (proof lines 18096-18103): for every quasi-compact quasi-separated object U of X_etale the map E -> R(X_K -> X)_*E|_{X_K} restricts to an isomorphism on cohomology by (1), and since every object of X_etale is covered by such U, the map itself is an isomorphism.
proof_roadmap: Use purely inseparable extensions and topological invariance to reduce to algebraically closed base fields.
Write the extension of algebraically closed fields as a filtered colimit of smooth algebras and apply smooth base change.
Spread the resulting identification from quasi-compact quasi-separated objects to all objects to get the isomorphism of sheaves.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for an extension of separably closed fields the cohomology of a torsion complex with invertible orders does not change, in the form of the two assertions (statement lines 18065-18076). The proof (proof lines 18078-18103) reduces to algebraically closed fields by topological invariance along purely inseparable extensions, applies smooth base change using the description of such an extension as a filtered colimit of smooth algebras, and then spreads the identification from quasi-compact quasi-separated objects to the isomorphism of sheaves. H2: one reduction and one base change application, written out.
